content.text: I now have access to the Trail API. It lists 119 Trails in total, and the onboarding Trail alone has 42 unresolved comments. I’m checking those existing findings against the current PR changes to avoid duplicating resolved or outdated feedback.

The inventory is complete: 88 open PRs map to 88 open Trails, and 45 PRs depend on another open PR. So far, three Trails report failing CI. Most Trail review runners have never run, so a zero-finding count is not evidence that those branches passed review.

I’ve confirmed the CI failure on #181 is the negative-control test addressed by #193. I’m now validating a few code-level concerns with small reproductions, including a fact-record size boundary and whether the new “safe” status check can block on a named pipe.

findings=[
(111,'Concurrent fact reclassification is lost during distillation','internal/cli/distill_cmd.go',2132,
'When another writer changes an existing fact’s kind while distillation is running, `rebaseFactsOntoDisk` preserves the older in-memory record. It adopts new IDs and retirement status but ignores other updates to existing IDs. A subsequent flush overwrites the concurrent reclassification despite taking the writer lock. This undercuts the PR’s concurrent-write preservation guarantee.',
'A test against the complete PR head wrote the same fact with `Kind="constraint"` and a later update timestamp, then called the real rebase helper. It returned an empty kind. The two existing concurrent-write/force regression tests pass.',
'Preserve concurrent edits to existing records with a three-way or field-aware merge. Add coverage for reclassification, provenance changes, and reactivation, while retaining the intended force-rebuild behavior.'),
(174,'Independent benchmark runs share agent state','benchmarks/agent-brain/brainmark/run_b.py',418,
'The new opaque agent-home path hashes only pair ID, arm, and repetition. Two separate result directories running the same cell resolve to the same persistent agent home. The adapters create that directory if needed and do not reset it, so session/configuration state can cross independent runs; concurrent runs also share it. This compromises benchmark isolation.',
'Invoked the exact production path functions with `/tmp/run-a/pair/no_brain` and `/tmp/run-b/pair/no_brain`, using the same pair, arm and repetition. Both returned the identical agent-home directory.',
'Include an opaque run-specific identity in the namespace, keep explicit resume semantics, and ensure a fresh attempt receives fresh state. Apply the fix before folding this child into PR #88.'),
(97,'The document-index health probe hangs on a named pipe','internal/cli/doc.go',226,
'The new status/doctor probe opens the declared index before checking whether it is a regular file. On Unix, opening `docs/index.json` as a FIFO blocks waiting for a writer, so the later regular-file guard is never reached. A health check can hang indefinitely on precisely the invalid filesystem object it should diagnose.',
'A probe using the exact production function and a temporary FIFO blocked until the test opened a writer to release it. The test cleans up the blocked operation.',
'Use a safe nonblocking open followed by descriptor-based regular-file validation. Carry the correction through descendants #101, #113 and #141.'),
(128,'The writer accepts an exact-limit record that the reader rejects','internal/factmerge/ndjson.go',94,
'The writer allows a serialized JSON record of exactly `MaxLineBytes` and appends a newline. The scanner’s maximum buffer is also `MaxLineBytes`, leaving no space to recognize that delimiter. Thus a successful write can produce a facts file that cannot be read back.',
'Ran a round-trip test against the production factmerge package with a JSON record of exactly 16,777,216 bytes. Writing succeeded; reading failed with a line-exceeds-maximum error.',
'Make reader and writer limits agree, accounting for the delimiter. Test just below, exactly at, and above the boundary. Descendants #129 and #140 inherit the issue.'),
(190,'Multiple colons still confuse semantic endpoint paths','internal/cli/semantic.go',1217,
'The new parser treats the first colon followed by a bare token as the path/kind boundary. For `dir:a:b/file.go:function:F`, it interprets `a` as the kind and returns `dir`. Valid paths with multiple colons therefore still receive the wrong ignore decision. The added single-colon case does not cover this ambiguity.',
'Called the exact endpoint/parser functions with `gh/a/b:Go:dir:a:b/file.go:function:F`. The parsed path was `dir`, not `dir:a:b/file.go`.',
'Use explicit endpoint path metadata or an unambiguous symbol-ID contract. Add multiple-colon cases and verify both inclusion and exclusion of relation endpoints.')]
